1b20ec04944e7732.summary: A small-group acting course for first-year students in the Schauspiel program, focused on scene work and basic performance practice. It is an internal course for the undergraduate acting curriculum.

7938c5895dede6d9.summary: Project supervision for first-semester master students working on a studio project at Ballhaus Ost, a Berlin theatre venue, within the stage design track of the Performing Arts faculty. The description is sparse, so the exact focus of the practical work is not stated.

df952fd617d59c7f.summary: Explores the relationship between static and moving typography through experimental motion design work in After Effects. Emphasis is on collaborative processes and students developing their own approach to motion design tools.

e6b3918d7a687298.summary: An internal editing and dramaturgy course in the Darstellende Kunst faculty's scenic writing track, where advanced students work on analytical reading and critique of dramatic texts. Little description is published, so the focus is inferred from the title and catalog path.

50bca4340db0c0bc.summary: A seminar on color theory and compositional principles within visual communication, aimed at building foundational design skills. The sparse record suggests a basic-level course for undergraduate design students.

7f85a6cdeb1d7907.summary: A seminar on developing story material and advising students on their narrative film projects, from idea and concept to script stage. The course sits in the narrative film class of the Fakultät Gestaltung's art and media area.

bfe6a9d796a9dd2f.summary: An internal course in dialogue technique for students of the Performing Arts faculty, placed within the scenic writing track at the undergraduate level. The description is empty, so the focus is inferred from the title and catalog path: writing convincing dialogue for scenes.

0a7fb6d069f7e117.summary: A cultural studies seminar that critically reads literature, pop culture and Deutschrap lyrics on sex, love, tenderness and body discourses. It examines female sextalk, reclaiming, intersectional feminism, racism and Islamic perspectives on sexuality.

00a837c61bf2839b.summary: A cultural studies seminar within the Studium Generale diversity program, where students read texts on power and structural inequality and lead a session with an artistic-discursive format. The title suggests a focus on 'Weiche Macht' (soft power) and its interplay with diversity and power structures.

a1c7f9b75500d8cf.summary: A public lecture series on the history of so-called guest-worker migration in Germany, its ties to religion, labour and art, and postmigrant memory culture. It connects these themes to Hip Hop, popular culture, gender and racism critique.

b8d98d1d879b06cc.summary: A block seminar examining how refrigeration and cryogenic technologies, used to preserve life, food, data and archives, intersect with colonial, capitalist and national interests and shape visions of future and survival on a warming planet. Readings, objects and media are analysed together, ending in a written or artistic-research final project.

f92da9cc83cf181b.summary: A block seminar examining "fabulation" as a critical, political and aesthetic method, tracing it from literary theory through Black, feminist and queer scholarship and art practice. It focuses on how fabulation imagines lives and worlds where archives are broken or erased.

7957d8ca9dccc9e4.summary: A seminar examining futures beyond repair, questioning dominant narratives of crisis, progress and the good life through artists' writings and theory from visual culture, decolonial, affect and queer studies. It asks how attachments to these narratives shape which futures seem possible or desirable.

3768e365c70be0b8.summary: A historical survey of humanity's attempts to build learning machines, from myths and early automata through Leibniz, Babbage, Lovelace and Turing to modern neural networks and large language models. It combines this history with practical AI literacy and questions whether 'artificial intelligence' is the right name for these systems.

e965f844b514287e.summary: A seminar that rethinks theatre and performance history by centring practices from the Global South and other marginalized contexts, questioning the categories and archives that shaped dominant narratives. It combines critical readings, audiovisual materials and practical exercises to treat performance both as an object of study and as a method for investigating memory and history.

412dd075c7a1069d.summary: A seminar exploring how art and education can act within postcolonial double binds of migration society, treating futurity as an aesthetic and political practice that opens new possibilities for thinking, perceiving and acting. It draws on theorists such as Mecheril, Muñoz, Spivak and Bhabha, with an online part and an intensive presential block in February 2027.

72a7c31b95691798.summary: A block seminar on Amazofuturism, a science-fiction and visual art current that imagines the Amazon's future in a technologized world while questioning colonial perspectives. It covers the history of colonialism and extractivism in the region, contemporary environmental struggles, and key literary and artistic practitioners, through readings and documentaries.

bddbf7e8ee0df3e6.summary: A seminar introducing systems thinking as an artistic and philosophical approach, examining how systemic, networked and collaborative methods can shape artistic practice and understanding of transition. Students discuss works by thinkers such as Manuel DeLanda, David Lynch, David Graeber and Robert Smithson, and broadcast outcomes as live DAB radio.

26e5f4b382cbf544.summary: Explores how different political time horizons (pre-modern, fascist, communist, liberal) are structured cognitively and how authoritarian movements exploit brain vulnerabilities around uncertainty and closure. Combines neuroscience and political readings with the development of performance art responses to illiberal time frames.

4e7e88a5451294a1.summary: A block seminar combining Lovis Heuss's un//masking zines and Angela Alves's Care Pods practice to explore neurodivergent artistic creation, access needs, rest, and collective reflection. It treats un//masking as a method for resisting neuronormative expectations in art-making.

90e9f72b38184415.summary: A block seminar on writing 'stories of success' that combines personal experience and positive journalism with literary techniques such as essay, autofiction and poetry. It aims to build hopeful, future-oriented writing as an alternative to doomscrolling.

d5fb94a029736c9a.summary: A theoretical-practical course exploring memes, memetics and memeplexes as cultural units of transmission, combining observation experiments with artistic concept development for memetic campaigns. Students work in small groups and present their concepts at a concluding congress.

de75a08368c1ac24.summary: A theory-practice seminar examining how public statues and monuments in Berlin encode power, gender, colonial and class narratives, followed by speculative artistic work on alternative forms of public memory. Students develop counter-monument proposals in a futurity studio format.

81f2e079b365a46a.summary: A contemplative seminar in which participants pick one personal routine and observe it across the semester alongside readings on habit and attention. Halfway through, they adopt a classmate's routine alongside their own, and the course closes with a finished piece built from the work.

4b61527aa9caaf9d.summary: A practice-based seminar that reexamines Henry Purcell's opera Dido and Aeneas as once-popular music about current themes, asking how FLINTA* and marginalized groups can reclaim their voices. Students sing, improvise, write texts and build short opera miniatures in an open form.

1b1182fd038ff3fa.summary: A hands-on seminar where students build personal artistic tools using AI coding agents, framed by Ivan Illich's notion of conviviality and critical discourse on artificial intelligence in contemporary art. It aims at tools that extend one's own artistic practice across photography, sound, sculpture, performance, writing or time-based media.

689caef5ae37fa7f.summary: A compact block seminar exploring art projects that combine meditation practice with aesthetic production and reception, including experiments and a final catalogue of exercises. Students attend a mandatory preparatory session and a retreat in Sauen, with application via motivation letter.

b10dc7cdda58c36c.summary: A interdisciplinary block seminar exploring panoramic views and horizons over Berlin as a basis for speculative utopian or dystopian visions of the future, combining cultural-historical readings on panoramas with drawing, photography, film and digital visualization experiments. Students develop their own artistic project around the idea of the sky over Berlin as a theatre of tomorrow.

da9fdcabaebc5a64.summary: A seminar on plein-air painting that treats outdoor painting as material, boundary-crossing and absurd practice rather than classic landscape art, combining art-historical examples with weekly outdoor painting sessions across Berlin in all weather. It ends with a shared exhibition, and no prior painting talent is required.

81fa423e4def897c.summary: A project seminar exploring how we relate to our surroundings through alternative love stories, producing short speculative video works and spatial narratives using 3D body scans combined with buildings, plants and other-than-human bodies. Participants attend the Love Is a Verb festival and conclude with a public presentation.

3c446b4c6afc3aca.summary: A block seminar on the 'lost form' method of multicolour screen printing, using mould, decay and fungal imagery as a way to explore irreversible, open-ended decisions. Students learn screen printing basics and produce several multi-colour prints alongside drawing experiments.

5ec669602a6cde88.summary: A project-based seminar exploring how the human body intersects with law, including reproductive rights, migration, protest, and warfare, and how art and aesthetics can question legal notions of truth, agency, and justice. Students co-curate a lecture series and practice-based workshops with lawyers and activists.

263d821806279b0f.summary: A collaborative workshop series in which composers and stage designers build small interactive systems linking sound, light, sensors, motors and electronics for concert, theatre and installation settings. Participants learn hands-on electronics such as kinetic sound, wireless MIDI controllers and responsive lighting, with no prior technical experience required.

8bdc7a7b0362c952.summary: A student-initiated interdisciplinary project seminar on first-person narration in contemporary culture, examining autofiction, autotheory, social media confessionals, novels, drama and essays through identity, authenticity and attention economy. It combines theory with writing workshops and performance practice, ending in a joint performance or reading.

d0d105ce42779ac0.summary: A cross-university project reframing the flâneur through the figure of the flâneuse, using Friedrichstraße in Berlin as a case to examine how bodies, power and exclusion shape urban space. Students combine somatic practice, textual work, design and theory in a shared research process across architecture, graphic/communication design and spatial strategies.

6430ecbc4caa063d.summary: An interdisciplinary project course where students from different UdK classes collaboratively develop time-based and performative artworks that challenge conventions such as the white cube, authorship and audience. It includes workshops on peer learning, performance, material practices, co-creation and artistic approaches to AI, culminating in a festival-like presentation.

2a44d65e211c1287.summary: A seminar on pedagogical observation of pupils, examining how observations and images shape teachers' judgments, inequality, and diagnostic labels in primary education. Students reflect on their own pedagogical gaze and test artistic, image-based documentation methods in art classes.

b6f18bfcc0fe9e2d.summary: A seminar treating urban commons as an ongoing social practice of opening, maintaining and negotiating shared spaces, with readings, visits to commoning projects in Berlin, and collective mapping and a city walk. Students from several UdK programs collaborate and document results in a booklet.

d3a8ded417d2a9af.summary: A project seminar where students confront online anxieties and overwhelming trends such as tradwife content, looksmaxxing, AI slop and the manosphere through humor and absurdity. Participants build an object or playful work, possibly a cyberdeck, and document it in a shared toolbox with a small exhibition.

ec6a5d0364f7007d.summary: A student-led interdisciplinary project exploring embroidery, conductive yarns and electronics to build interactive textile loudspeakers that turn body and fabric movement into sound. It pairs hands-on prototyping with critical reflection on craft, technology and the cultural history of loudspeakers.

2404b430041c0377.summary: An introduction to art education for primary school teachers, combining educational theory with reflection on students' own artistic practice. It prepares students for the practical semester and the grund_schule der künste teaching model.

ed23feb0b3d26179.summary: A interdisciplinary student-initiated project examining speed, control and consumption on Berlin's Kurfürstendamm through site-specific performance, sound work and interventions with speed cameras. Participants research the topic with experts in law, psychology, dramaturgy and sound mapping and present short collision performances at the end.

7fb3a8277c37cd08.summary: MAKE SHIFT is an interdisciplinary lecture and colloquium series for Visual Communication and Product Design master students at UdK, bringing international designers and researchers to discuss current discourses beyond the regular curriculum. Students also use the sessions to reflect on their master theses with external guests.

1bed2fcdb812ebbb.summary: A seminar on how art teaching projects emerge from artistic ideas and how pupils learn and what the teacher's role is, using practical examples. It includes mandatory school observation visits outside regular seminar times.

1c3e2d369835e21e.summary: A seminar on 21st-century phototheoretical texts focusing on photographic archives, examining debates about omissions and logics of archives as well as curatorial and artistic practices of counter-archives. Reading-based, supplemented by exhibition visits and discussion of photographic works.

e4976023d79b58d1.summary: A teaching-based course in the art education bachelor program centred on individual and group artistic work, including performative interventions and spontaneous, improvised creation. Assessment is through presenting one's own works and participating in group projects.

0c87721cb9820f29.summary: A reading seminar exploring the many meanings of 'aesthetic', from beauty and taste to sensory perception, and how their evaluations relate to one another. It also draws on images, practices and phenomena through research.

f99a25270e03cb7f.summary: A seminar on memetics, the study of how cultural patterns replicate, vary, and get selected, tracing the idea from biological evolution through imitation, neuroscience and media to contemporary phenomena like viruses, emojis and memecoins. It treats culture as an evolving ecosystem of self-propagating patterns.

b2d5f3a9e319d3be.summary: A historical and theoretical survey tracing ideas of artificial minds from ancient myths, automata and early algorithms through Leibniz, Lovelace, Turing and Shannon up to modern machine learning, language models and AI agents. It asks what these 'thinking machines' should be called and what they mean culturally.

c66e500162898bc3.summary: Preparation and implementation of inclusion-oriented artistic projects with a school class at the grund_schule der künste, focusing on children's aesthetic practices and ways of engaging with the world. Students combine their own artistic practice with a theory-based description and a reflective design of an artistic setting.

18dc7eeb9117bff5.summary: The seminar examines how artistic studio practice can support children's aesthetic self-education, looking at atmosphere and how a studio becomes a space for children's own questions and forms of expression. It combines artist-in-residence school projects with theoretical texts and reflection on participants' own studio work.

a0da161358d29ddf.summary: A block course in which students design and produce bookmark prototypes that intervene in library collections, marking colonial and decolonial passages to explore radically inclusive, shadow archives of Black, Indigenous, PoC and queer communities. The second phase develops a printed bookmark design and ends with happenings in campus libraries, grounded in readings on Black study, decolonising design and archive theory.

1895b303b50f2c4e.summary: A companion seminar accompanying the practical teaching semester of the UdK master's program for art teacher training at secondary schools and grammar schools. It supports student teachers in reflecting on their classroom practice during the placement.

e4410af107dc1853.summary: A practice-oriented seminar on power-critical and discrimination-sensitive art education, working through existing educational materials and tools. Students develop art- and action-oriented lesson plans and teaching strategies, building on a preparatory seminar.

ff184f18ab814e7a.summary: An introductory proseminar on the basics of academic work in art history and the methods of art studies, including reading exemplary texts, object-based exercises with originals, and an introduction to Western iconography. It is aimed mainly at first- and second-semester students in fine arts and teacher-training programs.

d7d3a95e5bb873fa.summary: A doctoral colloquium supporting ongoing dissertations at the UdK Fine Arts faculty, where candidates discuss supervision requests and progress. It is an administrative supervision format rather than a subject-matter course.

b5fe963b71c1ace6.summary: A seminar for student teachers in the art-education master's track that reflects theoretically on their experiences during the school practicum semester. Students complete a portfolio as the examination requirement.

839aa8dfc7069fde.summary: Introduces typography and type design as part of visual communication practice, covering letterform construction and the making of typefaces. The seminar is part of the graphic design bachelor track.

1cd98d143d1e6604.summary: A seminar on the intersection of art and publishing, likely examining books, zines and print as artistic and communicative media within a graphic design context. The description is missing, so this is inferred from the title, department and catalog path.

9d163f312dd87bb6.summary: A theory-based follow-up seminar reflecting on the practice semester completed in schools, for students training to teach art at primary level. It is a prerequisite-bound course within the teacher-training fachdidaktik module.

b021ce51111f8d87.summary: A project seminar on everyday and cherished objects in children's material worlds, examining things as actors and museums as educational spaces. Students develop an exhibition for pupils from a partner school within the UdK's primary-teacher art education context.

7ba9f2636df36a38.summary: The seminar examines contemporary artistic strategies that shift notions of work, medium, author and visibility, and explores how they can be translated into experimental art teaching formats. Students develop and test their own classroom ideas, discussing canon, participation, assessment and the evaluation of process-based or ephemeral works.

6515d7805abd4bb8.summary: A seminar on reading and writing texts in relation to their context within graphic design practice, likely addressing how written content and discourse frame visual communication work. The description is missing, so this is inferred from the title, department and catalog path.

f7fb0f2d64f2d95b.summary: A seminar on experimental typography centred on designing a lyric zine based on the poetry of Joolz Denby. It works through typographic experimentation applied to the layout and printing of a small publication.

45ad184df124bb3c.summary: A seminar on typography as a conceptual practice, using books about academic teaching as a starting point to explore how text hierarchy (headings H1 to H4) structures knowledge and argument. It sits within the typography lab of the Visual Communication bachelor program.

847642827e0b9666.summary: A seminar in the Visual Communication bachelor's elective track focused on methodological work for design practice, taught by Florian Schimanski. The published record gives no detailed description, so the specific methods covered are unconfirmed.

1fd0deb8d4bed7c3.summary: A seminar on visual editing practices in graphic and communication design, likely covering image selection, sequencing and editorial layout. The description is missing, so the scope is inferred from the title and catalog path.

ab59879f941cea1c.summary: A seminar on the tensions between artistic freedom and institutional demands in art education, examining how grading, taste, social background, and teacher position shape assessment of open-ended art tasks. It discusses art-didactic positions, teaching materials, and evaluation models, aiming at a reflected personal stance rather than a fixed rubric.

933b7e849366ed6d.summary: A seminar on the legal and contractual side of creative work, covering how ideas can be protected and how agreements with clients and collaborators are structured. It is aimed at visual communication students who need practical grounding in copyright and contracts.

29e9ff8f8fe48707.summary: A hands-on seminar in which participants make stop-motion animation films with varied materials and media, reflecting on their own aesthetic experiences. It connects these experiences to aesthetic education and children's aesthetic practices, aimed at future primary school teachers.

96013170f5b9be1e.summary: A hands-on printmaking workshop covering mechanical intaglio techniques without etching: copperplate engraving, drypoint and mezzotint, from preparing the plate through to printing. Emphasis is on craft precision, material-based thinking and developing independent printed works; no prior experience required.

e71d914a24fa03f6.summary: A seminar tracing the history of collaborations between artists, technologists and scientists from the 1950s onward, from E.A.T. and New Tendencies to contemporary artistic R&D. Students practice documenting and writing about artistic works and collaborative practices through weekly writing exercises and workshops.

78fd994d710ab035.summary: A block seminar examining the relationship between colonialism and antisemitism through debates on multidirectional memory, including Arendt, Césaire, Mbembe and Rothberg. It focuses on contested cases in contemporary art and curating, such as the documenta fifteen controversy and the Oyoun defunding, and on artistic practices of solidarity between Jewish and decolonial positions.

99b1bc9a62bf78ee.summary: The seminar examines how moving images shape places through perspective, montage, sound and omission, drawing on Doreen Massey's relational concept of place and Trinh T. Minh-ha's critique of documentary. Students analyse contemporary film and video works and discuss production with invited artists.

85ffaec9d7f52490.summary: A seminar teaching practical methods for spatial representation, combining 2D drawing with experimental 3D modelling and analogue making skills within a spatial design and exhibition design context. The semester theme 'Spectral Traces' is introduced at a launch event rather than in the catalog text.

986d394b660e1b1c.summary: A weekend intensive workshop on how fakes, deepfakes and AI-generated identities blur the line between real and fake, and how artists can use fake strategies. Participants build fictional identities and narrative artifacts and develop them into a collaborative media performance.

347af25b7da0b6a5.summary: Introduces art-education positions across historical, affective-performative and transcultural clusters, focusing on aesthetic-artistic learning processes and the reflective teacher role. Students design and enact aesthetic learning settings using three core teaching practices through reenactments, as preparation for a teaching-focused art didactics module.

40a394a0ce6bbff6.summary: A project and colloquium for teacher-trainee artists that deepens art education and art mediation through cultural, phenomenological, postdigital, posthumanist and spatial theory. Students develop their own artistic-educational project, grounded in an exhibition or artwork and in two or more theoretical positions, for presentation and school-context evaluation.

1a27e81b10a86cee.summary: A theoretical seminar for future art teachers examining the tensions between art education and school structures, such as curricula and grading, using Helsper's antinomies of pedagogical action. It asks how art lessons can still enable open, aesthetic experiences, including questions of diversity and inclusion.

656fae1a117858f6.summary: A supervision seminar accompanying student teachers during their practicum semester in art education at secondary schools and gymnasiums. It is part of the teacher-training master's module for fine arts and focuses on reflecting classroom practice.

ffb6590e6391c665.summary: An introductory seminar on art education (Kunstdidaktik) for future teachers, examining how art can be mediated and which situated, art-adjacent practices and modes of showing art enable subjective access and aesthetic processes in school art lessons. It reflects on the teacher's own situatedness, institutional framing, space, materiality and mediality through theory and hands-on experimentation.

f71472bdc7372542.summary: A two-block intensive workshop in which participants develop two independent artistic or cultural project proposals, moving from contextual research and concept development to planning, budgeting, timelines, roles and professional presentation. It uses visual mapping tools such as process maps, mood boards and workflows, and explores co-creation with AI.

a8f33948121270fa.summary: A seminar introducing art mediation as a reflexive, power-critical and sometimes artistic practice, centered on unlearning, performativity and embodiment to interrupt inherited knowledge orders. It explores how mediation can make hegemonic knowledge visible and open spaces for collective knowledge production.

bd385ba540401fcd.summary: An introductory seminar on philosophy and aesthetics examining how art and philosophy can serve as critical, resistant practices amid global political crises. It focuses on Kant's concept of the aesthetic subject and its Marxist and queer-feminist politicization in the 20th century.

e9b7c53b808869f1.summary: A seminar introducing art education as a reflexive, power-critical and sometimes artistic practice, centered on unlearning, performativity and embodiment in learning processes. Students test site-specific mediation strategies in out-of-school venues such as exhibitions, theatre and digital spaces using performance art, post-internet art education, action research and mapping.

75df5f80c65258b3.summary: A project colloquium where postgraduate art students present and discuss their artistic projects and ongoing practice, from concept and theory through realization to evaluation. Topics range from memory culture and investigative approaches to current art, politics and pop culture.

0e72230818a889a1.summary: Students carry out independent artistic projects in the textile medium within the open textile workshop, with optional loom reservation and individual project supervision. The course deepens artistic practice with textiles through self-directed making, supported by prior consultation and sketches.

e96512ce6862b08a.summary: An accompanying seminar for the practical teaching semester of the lateral-entry art teacher training for secondary schools and gymnasiums at UdK. It supports student teachers reflecting on and organizing their classroom practice in art education.

fd0583fe91d7950c.summary: An introductory exercise on research methods in art education, covering how research questions arise from practice and how to apply qualitative content and image analysis. It also addresses linking empirical data with theory and structuring an academic research project.

5130f8bdf3246961.summary: An introductory seminar on research methods in art education, covering how art-pedagogical research questions arise and how to study them with qualitative content and image analysis. It also addresses linking practical teaching experience with theory and organising a research project.

8c38347880770144.summary: A seminar on aesthetic research as a core approach for art teaching in secondary schools, combining artistic-research methods with theoretical texts and the design of classroom formats. Students plan, test and reflect on process-oriented, self-directed learning and the teacher's role.

6b2894940a33378b.summary: A three-day hands-on workshop on making plant-based pigments and paints for textiles, including lake pigments mixed with binders and washable colour pastes. The paints are also suited to stencils and stamping techniques.

c9c0d693b8b6097a.summary: A block seminar examining the relationships between play, art and education, including play theory, playful learning, gamification in schools and what a pedagogy of play offers art teaching. Students read foundational texts on play theory and pedagogy and develop their own game-based learning concepts.

ee019e1d0de338b6.summary: Examines AI art within the longer history of automation, computation, cybernetics and algorithmic art, from automata and Harold Cohen's AARON to GANs and contemporary generative models. It addresses changing notions of agency, authorship, creativity and originality alongside copyright, labour, datasets, bias and environmental costs.

f230e37c04e38cc2.summary: The course treats sound as material, medium and spatial practice, surveying electronic music and sound art through analysis of works and writings. Students make individual projects using DAWs, field recording, multichannel audio and installation methods, with workshops at the artist-run space Errant Sound in Berlin.

c6016ed76d1cb418.summary: The seminar examines how visual artists and musicians translate sound, performance and movement into material forms such as sculpture, drawing, notation and scores, and how these works preserve ephemeral sound. It studies artworks, archival materials and performance documentation, including works by Peter Brötzmann and Jason Moran.

7062d3b1844d0ebf.summary: A seminar on the exhibition and discourse surrounding The Istanbul Pavilion of the Gaza Biennale, examining its artworks, poetry, political theory and networked structures. Students collaboratively produce a publication on the pavilion's nomadic afterlife for presentation at the Sharjah Biennale.

f7f635043b56c929.summary: A seminar examining documenta as an exhibition series that shapes how art relates to its historical and political moment, tracing selected editions from 1955 onward and their curatorial models, practices and debates. Particular attention goes to documenta fifteen, its collective and artist-led approach, and the controversies surrounding it.

58f29303565e756b.summary: A seminar-style course in which students develop artistic and art-research responses to the Endangered Languages Archive (ELAR) and the wider question of language endangerment, colonial extraction, and documentation. It includes preparing and supporting an ELAR exhibition at the Kommunikationsmuseum Berlin and a guest visit by sound artist Jamie Perera.

db39ffa6c9b03cfa.summary: A seminar introducing durational contemplation, a place-responsive artistic practice in which students craft long-duration performances within chosen Berlin sites, guided by theories of ritual, improvisation and film works on urban history. Students work in mentor-mentee partnerships with visiting US bachelor students over an intensive six-week period.

b23e21d0cf6635d2.summary: A seminar on using the precision of language to articulate and clarify one's own artistic work, identify conceptual gaps, and distill a personal thread. It culminates in writing an artist statement, produced without AI tools and built through dialogue.

a1077e5f3800a3ab.summary: A seminar on whether 'art' in the singular is a meaningful category, tracing the dissolution of boundaries between genres and media from the avant-gardes through 1960s practices like Fluxus, Land Art and Direct Cinema to performance, video and digital public spheres. It combines aesthetic theory with critical analysis of concepts such as autonomy, work, medium and genre.

02b50f7df7795f79.summary: A hands-on workshop on Adobe Lightroom covering its structure, catalog-based image management, and the Develop module for RAW conversion and image optimization. It is aimed at students already experienced with digital image editing.

be46c71afdab377d.summary: A cross-institutional project seminar revisits Sigmar Polke's 1986 Venice Biennale installation ATHANOR through the themes of technology, time and materiality, linking its works to climate change, resource scarcity and digitalisation. Students produce audio, text and image contributions for a digital archive.

012046cb660ce038.summary: A seminar examining Black German cinema and film history, using the 2007 Berlinale Panorama 'NEUE BILDER' program as a case study of how Black filmmakers working in Germany from the 1960s to 1990s were overlooked in screenings and restorations. It combines projection studies, archival research and key texts on Black German cultural production, with screenings and discussions with invited filmmakers and scholars.

f4ac4db960e9a2cb.summary: A hands-on workshop on plaster as a material, covering basic material knowledge, plaster casting, moulding and pouring techniques, and surface finishing. Sessions combine short theory blocks with practical exercises in the UdK workshop.

c98156a3720d8acc.summary: A seminar comparing Renaissance art north and south of the Alps, examining exchange, transformation and regional distinctiveness through works in the Berlin Gemäldegalerie and Bode-Museum. Topics include nature observation, perspective, the nude and religious imagery.

0f62026b873a7309.summary: A block course concluding a project on radically inclusive and decolonial archives, in which students design and print bookmarks to intervene in library collections at IfKiK and HfS. It draws on Harney and Moten, Tunstall's Decolonising Design, and Derrida's Archive Fever.

880cd478dd76cefc.summary: A teacher-training seminar on material and materiality in art education, examining how materials shape learning and artistic practice in school art lessons. Students document and reflect on their own learning and research in a portfolio.

69cfd6ea7c4579b4.summary: A seminar on 1960s avant-garde performance and sculpture, examining how the Judson Dance Theater and Franz Erhard Walther reconfigured the relations between body, object, audience and artist. It also questions hierarchical performance formats and gender norms and traces their relevance to contemporary participatory and body-based art.

4ed1f86ae2f45972.summary: A theory-practice seminar on the history of Berlin's municipal galleries as urban cultural infrastructure, examining their institutional development and cultural-policy role. Students work with primary archival sources from several municipal gallery archives and produce collective outputs such as an audio guide or small publication.

a755f495d1b54061.summary: Hands-on introduction to building virtual and mixed reality worlds, covering spatial design, found and modeled 3D objects, lighting and sound, and VR sculpting tools. Students learn basics of the Unity game engine and collaboratively assemble a walkable shared VR environment.

39579c1386c2ffa2.summary: A three-day introductory block seminar on stop-motion animation covering basic techniques, the workshop's animation rostrum, the Dragonframe software, and post-production with sound and editing. The course also includes a short introduction to Blender for placing and staging existing 3D models in virtual scenes.

b41e41aea535d4dc.summary: A colloquium where students in the postgraduate Art in Context program discuss their current artistic practice, focusing on art mediation with social groups and institutions and on discrimination-critical educational work. It offers brainstorming, critical feedback, and individual support on project development, funding, and collaboration.

14d9889ba951eaac.summary: A seminar supplementing an art project colloquium on intervention in public and social space, focused on funding and resource acquisition for artistic projects. Students research funding sources, analyze models of artistic entrepreneurship, and develop an individual financing strategy with a grant application and a cooperation request.

ce61b74c4065ab22.summary: An introductory hands-on workshop to Blender for students without 3D experience, covering scene setup with existing models, lighting, cameras, composition, basic animation and rendering. It moves from staging found models toward modifying and building simple objects for artistic projects.

2524fc8c08f954e7.summary: A theoretical-practical course on bodies, migration, sisterhood and collective memory, developed around the exhibition ENCOUNTERS by Tanja Ostojić at Kunstraum Kreuzberg. Students co-create a public 'Human Library' event and their own artistic interventions or mediation formats presented in the 'Schwester Kiosk' social space.

2b99dd6d128b9bb5.summary: Examines the relationship between ethics and aesthetics in urban and socially engaged art practice, and how the notion of community can be rethought through participatory, collaborative and micro-interventionist projects in a neighborhood setting. Students analyze reference projects and develop their own interventions in a cooperative shop run with S27 Kunst und Bildung.

9a0853a00181b338.summary: A project colloquium for postgraduate art students that critically reviews their own media art projects in form, concept and content. It centers on moving images in installation, public space, exhibition and online contexts, including film, video, sound and performance.

76c5e084c154270e.summary: Introductory phonetics training for first-year acting students within the breath, voice, speech and singing track of the drama faculty. The course focuses on speech sounds and articulation as foundations for vocal work on stage.

e8850bb0f41fe610.summary: Internal verse-speaking training for second-year acting students in the Atem-Stimme-Sprechen-Singen track, focusing on poetry recitation within the undergraduate acting curriculum. The sparse record gives no detailed content beyond the title and catalog placement.

2d7e078c18553845.summary: A companion seminar for art teacher trainees in a practicum semester, reflecting on their own classroom experience in secondary art education. It covers planning, running and evaluating art lessons, school visits, and developing a personal art-pedagogical self-concept through a academic portfolio.

6245cf01aa180e8b.summary: The seminar introduces artistic works from the last five decades that address site-specificity and concrete local conditions, and examines their relevance for architectural design. It runs as a block seminar over two weekends in the winter semester after two preparatory sessions.

fc3a5cf94b691f41.summary: A colloquium for teacher-training students in the art-teaching Quereinstieg master, reflecting jointly on their portfolio and the research question developed during their teaching practicum semester. Students must register by email and submit a 12-page academic portfolio.

a3888b4f6f505bde.summary: A hands-on workshop on translating sculptures into wax, covering the basics of wax materials alongside molding techniques (silicone skins, plaster support molds) and wax casting. Students also practice direct modeling and forming in wax.

8ec36789386bb88f.summary: A seminar on the visual and audio-visual grammar of film, examining how cuts, fades, freeze frames, faces, gestures and sound shape what a shot shows, withholds and means. Students are asked to apply this grammar to produce their own audio-visual work.

b89d6cd5a735a8c9.summary: A compact hands-on seminar introducing digital color correction and color grading for film and video, with DaVinci Resolve as the main tool. It also covers a full green-screen workflow, from studio setup and recording to chroma keying.

5cb01e679322c2f1.summary: A workshop seminar exploring play as an aesthetic practice, focusing on collaborative narrative role-playing games descended from 1970s adventure and role-playing traditions and their links to children's play. It examines narrative freedom and self-education from the perspective of the child, within a teacher-training context for primary school music and art.

dfe92616c4c75284.summary: A hands-on workshop on forming and modelling with papier-mâché, covering material basics, support structures with wire and paper, and surface finishing. Direct shaping is taught without mould-casting techniques.

d1091a4dc9914326.summary: Introduces power-critical and discrimination-sensitive perspectives in art education, examining how hegemonic structures, diversity, visual cultures and representation shape teaching content and practice. Students reflect critically on their own positionality and on social constructions such as gender, sexuality, disability, class and racialization.

1c27f5046ada1366.summary: A seminar on time-based art practices using contemporary technologies, within the UdK Fachklasse for time-based art in the art and media track. The description is sparse, so the specific technical focus is not stated.

cc6deef6e65b9ca0.summary: A two-semester interdisciplinary seminar with UdK and Ernst Busch students using Berlin's 1987 IBA Frauenblock housing project as a case study for feminist artistic research into how power relations shape space and bodies. Students develop experimental film and choreographic works that imagine and make visible body movement beyond patriarchal spatial orders.

a95fc60b37e2c11f.summary: Explores aesthetic experience in childhood as the basis for aesthetic education in primary school, combining artistic practice, discussion, reading and autobiographical writing. It engages childhood research, developmental psychology models of aesthetic education, and participants' own childhood memories as preparation for teaching.

51468e8980b92ff9.summary: Internal group class for first-year acting students in breath, voice, speech and singing training within the Schauspiel undergraduate program. The record gives no further detail on specific exercises or content.

432e30f296f16e6d.summary: A seminar on musical form (Formenlehre) within the artistic-pedagogical master's program in music theory, examining structural principles of musical compositions. Taught as the main artistic-theoretical module for students of the KPA profile.

977c124d8c402038.summary: A block seminar on aesthetic experience in childhood within the arts, offered as part of the music teacher training introduction module (MÄErz). Participation requires prior registration by email with the lecturer.

9f78e23fadae10bd.summary: A seminar in which participants create 10-second silent video pieces for digital advertising displays in Berlin U-Bahn stations, exploring the boundary between art and advertising and the formal constraints of public digital screens. The course combines theoretical research on public-space art with a practical production and presentation cycle ending in a screening.

1c667af8eb17b5b3.summary: A two-day workshop within a broader AI literacy course for Bachelor and Master students, focusing on text-generating AI systems and their use in artistic and academic contexts. The course is part of the Studium Generale and offers 4 ECTS credits.

712ebafacf2c064f.summary: Explores video beyond conventional filmmaking for installations and performance, including real-time multi-channel mixing, live-stream manipulation, and camera-based tracking of colour or motion to control other video. Students study artistic examples and build small practical projects.

e2075e08e4140576.summary: A practice-based painting course exploring how colour on a flat surface can create illusions of space and bodies, and how paint can extend into three-dimensional space. It also reflects on artistic process, chance, control, concept and creative crises through contemporary artistic positions.

5bb6ea04c6f83fb6.summary: The seminar explores how fleeting, ephemeral moments can be captured and transformed into printed objects, touching on archiving practices in visual communication. Students work on translating transient experiences into lasting printed form.

ba50854159533405.summary: Students study how everyday objects, materials and routines in shared public spaces such as libraries, train stations and universities can function as communication media. They design and build a 1:1 site-specific intervention that addresses a public concern and test its real effects.

0ef782c7ff490c0d.summary: A philosophical and aesthetic seminar examining beauty and love as affective, political forces that shape perception, desire and forms of togetherness, using philosophy, literature and art in a constellation-based rather than chronological approach. It addresses gender, body, class and colonial orders alongside care, intimacy and imagination.

dfe2659518cb405e.summary: Individual one-on-one advising for artists working on their own projects, focusing on how artistic idea, material choice, painting technique and visual effect interact. Covers material and process questions, developing a personal painterly language, and historical and contemporary painting techniques.

c628d8035bee6601.summary: The seminar explores the aesthetic and performative dimensions of law and asks what artistic strategies can be developed in response to legal structures. It brings together students from the Art in Context and HZT Solo/Dance/Authorship master's programs.

527596ef6b6b7fe3.summary: A seminar introducing the foundations and positions of art education (Kunstpädagogik) as part of a teacher-training module on theoretical subject didactics. Registration by email is mandatory before enrolling.

27d90324bc96deeb.summary: An introductory practice-oriented course on the foundations of installation art, exploring the interplay of space, object, materiality and viewer perception. Students visit current exhibitions and translate their findings into installative works.

54e84a3f5497ea1c.summary: An introductory seminar on art education (Kunstvermittlung) for prospective art teachers, examining how situated, subject-oriented approaches to showing and mediating art can provoke aesthetic processes in school art classes. It reflects on the teacher's own situatedness, institutional framing, space, materiality and mediality through theory and practical trials.

b92548b465b55826.summary: A free-drawing seminar focusing on basics and experiments in drawing, with excursions and critique sessions to deepen sensitivity to one's own drawing practice. Architecture and urban studies are also planned.

1491dc1988ea5856.summary: A block seminar on curating and guiding gallery visits as art-historical methods, where students build thematic tours of Renaissance paintings at the Berlin Gemäldegalerie. It draws on iconography, gender studies and political history to examine 15th–16th century European art critically.

8a79740a38fc31fe.summary: A practice-based seminar treating access (barrier reduction) as a generative artistic and curatorial practice rather than a retrofit, exploring creative captions, poetic audio description, and crip-time-friendly installations. Students work through Disability Arts positions and Critical Access theory alongside their own unfinished projects.

f15bb3deb007c2e3.summary: A hands-on introduction to film production practice at the UdK AV-Werkstatt, covering digital cameras, sound and lighting equipment through short theory units and practical exercises. Students also discuss their own film project questions and gain equipment access qualification.

984e442ef1c71b7f.summary: Explores what drawing can be as a medium, covering a wide range of techniques from hatching and single-line work to frottage, notation, sketching, life drawing, and naturalistic rendering. It also prepares drawings for further use in printmaking.

e1eedfdfc1971296.summary: A project seminar with a five-day block at the former Ravensbrück women's concentration camp, using artistic research and archive materials to examine visibility, refusal and positioning in relation to memory and the nearby town of Fürstenberg/Havel. It also covers critical reading on archival power and mediation practices in art.

63f0268449ba38fd.summary: Students study drawing as a medium by working directly from original old master paintings in museums, examining composition, painting structure and handling. The focus is on looking at originals and translating them into drawings.

94784de77239551e.summary: A colloquium supporting BA and MA thesis writing through discussion of independent academic research foundations, argumentation, outlines, abstracts, and methodological difficulties. It also offers help with topic selection for students in the fine arts teacher-training master's module.

b63f4bee87c1ad3b.summary: A seminar on architectural and built-environment education (Baukulturelle Bildung), exploring how people perceive, question and mediate places through aesthetic experience and artistic research. Students develop their own teaching practice using concrete urban sites as starting points for exploration.

4a382f65ab6a4d61.summary: A block seminar examining the concept of apocalypse in its original sense of 'revelation', asking how philosophy and the arts can engage with present-day visions of catastrophe such as climate collapse, nuclear war and AI risk. Readings include Günther Anders, Walter Benjamin, Antonin Artaud and Susan Sontag, ending with a film discussion with its artists.

cd000f56e0e6b4d8.summary: The seminar teaches material forensics, using life cycle assessment and environmental indicators such as global warming potential, acidification and water use to uncover the hidden histories of building materials. Students apply these life cycle analyses to real building projects and to their own design projects as a generative design tool.

719a4d0dbaaa95e0.summary: An orientation day for the Grundlehre (foundation year) in Fine Arts at UdK, covering welcome remarks, organizational matters, studio tours, and an informal get-together with tutors. It introduces first-year students to the studio practice of the foundation program.

ab8c37a6f473d7df.summary: A two-semester architecture design studio that diagnoses 'overheated' systems such as logistics centres, server farms and industrial zones through cybernetics, systems theory and actor-network theory. Students build diagrammatic research, AI-assisted scenarios and spatial interventions that address the body, subject and living environment.

bd43f1c8f7525779.summary: An introductory seminar on the relationship between art and science, tracing its historical and philosophical development up to current debates about artistic and scientific research. It also examines how art engages with social and historical trauma, memorial forms, and the methods of historiography and other disciplines.

48e9ad541e34fb89.summary: A large plenary group session within the fine arts foundation studies, part of the studio practice (Atelierpraxis) curriculum at UdK. The description is empty, so the content is inferred from the title and catalog path only.

cb082f7486886733.summary: A theoretical-practical course at the UdK's Art in Context master's track that appears to be linked to a symposium format, likely covering the organisation and presentation of an art-related event. The description is missing, so the exact content is inferred from the title and catalog path.

b4033852499e02f8.summary: A seminar exploring low-resource, mobile and decentralized approaches to artistic instruments, installations and performance systems as an alternative to high-power, big-tech computing. It also covers small-data machine learning and just-in-time programming for real-time interactive performance.

b572cb2a6cbdf590.summary: A seminar on visual storytelling in which students develop scenes from the image itself, exploring how light, composition, perspective, camera movement and shot choice shape atmosphere, characters and emotion. Practical exercises with concrete scenes aim to move beyond established cinematic conventions.

aed3a7c00e1920cb.summary: A seminar on conscious listening and representation in audio practice, asking how personal and social narratives can be built and exhibited without reproducing problematic modes of representation. Students collect field recordings, narrative fragments and interviews and reassemble them into dramaturgical compositions using urban music production techniques like sampling, beats and audio effects.

a70027ab0c9b499b.summary: A writing workshop that opens a semester of short film projects, developing characters, situations and narrative approaches from personal observations and memories about love. Students draft screenplay material through focused writing exercises, character work and group readings.

87fa9a7380679ae3.summary: A seminar on staging and relationships in film, starting with a writing workshop that turns personal observations and memories about love into characters, situations and story approaches for short film projects. It focuses on how a feeling or recollection becomes a cinematic scene through writing exercises and figure work.

4e026fe237f436b1.summary: A seminar within the New Media class of visual communication at UdK Berlin, framed around learning through inquiry. The description is empty, so the specific content and methods are not stated.

8fb8d9834eb85413.summary: The seminar examines editing and post-production as core storytelling tools, covering how rhythm, timing, perspective, music and sound design shape narrative and emotional effect. It also introduces VFX, compositing and online finishing to develop visual language in the post-production stage.

59bf53e561230ff0.summary: Explores light as a material for spatial design, examining how illumination shapes perception, atmosphere and the experience of space. The seminar sits within a New Media class in the Visual Communication bachelor program.

0ba8992a35e052b0.summary: A practice-based film course exploring documentary filmmaking methods such as research, observation, location scouting and working with protagonists. Students produce short documentary miniatures or films on work and labour, in forms ranging from direct cinema to essay or interview film.

c16c9009bedc9ea8.summary: The seminar examines different concepts of space and their role in artistic practice, focusing on installation and site-related working methods. It develops an expanded notion of site that includes social, historical and institutional contexts, combining practical exercises inside and outside the UdK with students' own projects.

10bbed79540e3984.summary: A hands-on seminar in which participants build their own personal digital tools with AI coding agents, guided by Ivan Illich's notion of conviviality, while critically examining the politics and limits of LLM technology. The tools are meant to extend individual artistic practices across photography, sound, sculpture, performance, writing and time-based media.

3b98c5e8dd25523e.summary: A seminar examining autofiction, autotheory, and other self-narrative forms in contemporary culture, from social media confessionals to novels, drama, and essays. Students trace the historical formation of the modern individual as subject and object of narration and write their own performative texts in workshops culminating in a showing.

38242db52f9e20d1.summary: A block seminar on creative writing that explores constructive, future-oriented storytelling by combining personal experience with positive journalism. Participants try out literary forms such as essay, autofiction and poetry, drawing on texts by established authors.

0f910fd4b0d4a827.summary: A weekly outdoor painting seminar that revisits plein-air practice beyond its classical landscape tradition, exploring material, boundary-crossing and absurd forms of painting in Berlin's urban space. Students work with field easels and canvases in all weather, ending with a shared exhibition.

574935f76d484f3f.summary: A block seminar exploring art projects that combine meditation practice with aesthetic practice, examining how meditative states can be reached and what meditative aspects exist in both artistic production and reception. Students run progressive meditation experiments during a retreat and compile a practice catalogue of exercises.

c6a9926268ba0fe5.summary: A Studium Generale ring seminar exploring how generative AI reshapes authorship, creativity, and responsibility in art, with guest artists and experts presenting work that makes opaque AI systems visible and hackable. It includes hands-on exercises and excursions to AI research centres in Berlin.

19d0cad7c1709146.summary: A block seminar combining Lovis Heuss's un//masking zine methodology with Angela Alves's Care Pods practice to explore neurodivergent artistic processes, access needs, rest and collective reflection. Designed especially for neurodivergent participants, it treats care and solidarity as part of artistic method.

ab99aa79fd2c576a.summary: A hands-on intensive workshop on how fakes, from deepfakes to fictional identities, blur the line between real and fake, with participants creating fake personas and narrative artifacts for a collaborative media performance. It uses media analysis and AI model experimentation to explore fakes as a generative artistic force.

dcfa1d6485b6b8b6.summary: A seminar examining the history of politically motivated art in public space, from the Living Theatre and Beuys to Pussy Riot and Zentrum für politische Schönheit, followed by small-group projects designing costume, performance and poster interventions for urban space. It combines reading and visual analysis with discussion of which futures public art should imagine.

6fca0dff87b7aabf.summary: A five-session seminar that approaches opera as once-popular music theatre, using Purcell's Dido and Aeneas as a starting point to explore voice, gender, and marginalized perspectives through listening, vocal practice, improvisation, and creating short original opera miniatures. No prior musical training is required.

bfaa2875b22a7998.summary: A contemplative seminar in which each participant chooses one personal routine, logs it across the semester, and then temporarily adopts a peer's routine alongside their own. Readings on habit and attention are paired with in-room experiments, culminating in a finished piece and a closing exhibition.

ca18df419fa950d1.summary: A block seminar exploring panoramic and horizon views over Berlin through drawing, photography and film, developing utopian or dystopian constructions of possible futures. Students create their own artistic work on deep pictorial space and wide formats, with bilingual German/English teaching.

880bd9f449c17fb6.summary: A two-part intensive workshop guiding participants from an artistic or cultural idea through contextual research, concept development, and visual process mapping to a professionally presentable project proposal. The second block adds planning, budgeting, timelines, roles, and professional presentation, with optional exploration of AI co-creation.

395ab793f23f25f4.summary: An intensive workshop on re-working materials and objects left behind by the deceased into future-facing memorial pieces, mainly through textiles and garments. It combines case studies, material theory, a short lecture on grief, and studio practice to develop a personal methodology.

a8fca211d5d82491.summary: A seminar examining the Enlightenment from its origins to the current rise of neoreactionary 'Dark Enlightenment' ideology in tech circles, including longtermism. It studies artistic engagements with enlightenment movements and counter-movements through critical, decolonial and queer-feminist theory.

43eb5a8380942f12.summary: A block seminar exploring Amazofuturism, a science-fiction and art movement that imagines the future of the Amazon region in a technologized world while questioning colonial perspectives. It covers the genre's origins, key literary and visual artists, and the history of colonialism and extractivism in the region.

088013e61bf94f48.summary: A block seminar examining the Vilém Flusser Archive at UdK and the transmediale festival, both marking anniversaries in 2027, and the question of what archives are for and how they resist decay. It combines meetings with transmediale curators, a McLuhan lecture and festival visits.

11ffa5884e384ee6.summary: A bilingual seminar examining how artists and theorists in visual culture, decolonial, affect and queer theory reframe repair, asking how narratives like crisis, progress and the good life shape which futures seem possible. Students write responses and an evolving text on imagining futures beyond reparative thinking.

16fef03dcc4faf52.summary: A block seminar tracing the history of fabulation as a critical, political and aesthetic method, from literary theory to its use by Black scholars, feminist writers and queer artists. It examines how fabulation imagines lives and worlds where archives are broken or erased, using readings, screenings and case studies.

554e5444df273ba3.summary: A two-part block seminar examining 'soft power' as a concept of influence through culture, including how art such as biennials serves national and diplomatic interests. Students read foundational theory and then develop artistic-discursive responses in small groups at an art association.

185e1a2a884f21b4.summary: A English-language seminar introducing systems thinking as an artistic and philosophical approach, examining how transitions across physics, bodies, economies and nation states call for networked, collaborative methods. Students read thinkers such as DeLanda, Graeber, Macy and Smithson and prepare material broadcast on live DAB radio.

c646b4ee418c4406.summary: A critical seminar that rethinks theatre and performance history by centring practices from the Global South and other marginalized contexts, questioning the categories and archives of dominant historiography. It combines readings, discussion, audiovisual analysis and practical exercises, treating performance both as an object of study and as a method for engaging memory and history.
